clue.text: I must leave leading cook

indicators.note: must leave says a letter has to depart from the word before it

parts.note: a leading figure is the chief one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces they must quit their top job in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' looks like it describes the cook, but it gives CHIEF; 'must leave' takes the I out.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional kitchen's cook is called by this title, from the French word for head.

clue.text: Trouble opening up in temple

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a gap is an opening

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong at the opening of a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ADOGAP around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower found in Buddhist and Hindu religious sites in Asia is a kind of temple.

clue.text: Mix-up involving plastic card, so ready money required

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hash is a muddle or mix-up

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters of card are reshaped

explanation.surface: A credit card fails, so the shopper must pay in notes and coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic card' reads as a credit card, but 'plastic' is the anagram signal, making RDCA, which goes inside HASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash in hand, available immediately, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: Braved winds heroically, say

indicators.note: winds, as a verb, means twists about, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bravely faced the gales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like a noun for the weather, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroically is a word that modifies a verb, an example of this part of speech, as 'say' shows.

clue.text: Force spring in lock in unlawful act

indicators.note: to force one thing into another is to push it inside
in says where the spring is pushed: into the lock

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar forces a spring mechanism in a door lock to break in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a door lock and a metal spring, but the lock is of hair and the spring is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering land without the right to is a wrongful act in law.

clue.text: Head of department is member to win over

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A department head is a staff member whose job is to win people round.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone so that their hostility goes is to win them over.

clue.text: Gala pie, ultimately, after endless cheese

indicators.note: after puts the pie's letter behind the cheese
endless means the last letter of the cheese is lost

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word pie

explanation.surface: At a gala, a pie is served after the cheese course.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive outdoor event, such as a village fair with stalls.

clue.text: Careless fellow caught out by chance

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught leaves the fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hazard means chance or risk

explanation.surface: A sloppy batsman is caught out by a stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' reads as one cricket phrase, but 'out' deletes C from CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done haphazardly is done without care or order, so slapdash.

clue.text: End use

definitions.meaning: an end is an aim or goal
the use of a thing is its function

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side; the surface reads as a single instruction to stop using something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an aim one strives for and the function something serves are covered by this word.

clue.text: Put up beams in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Stage crew hoist the lighting beams in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something or erect it is to put it up.

clue.text: Desert contains nutrients? Really!

indicators.note: contains says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: to forsake is to desert
the goodness in food is its nutrients

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished that a desert has any nutrients at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand, but it is the verb, FORSAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exasperated exclamation of disbelief, like 'Really!', is this phrase.

clue.text: Model of a scene I love in play

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a drama is a play
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An actor says how much they love the miniature set in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional miniature tableau, as in a museum, is this kind of display.

clue.text: Follow mother's belief

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
ma is mother, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A child is told to follow what their mother believes.
explanation.definitionFit: A firmly held principle or doctrine laid down as true is a belief of this kind.

clue.text: Famous cricketer, wicked guy bagging runs

indicators.note: bagging means pocketing, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: bad means wicked
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a man is a guy

explanation.surface: A villainous player piles up runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was an Australian batsman with the highest Test average ever recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Donald of this surname is widely held to be the greatest batsman in the game's history.

clue.text: Exposed, king in small valley, climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top
in places the king inside the valley

parts.note: a dean, or dene, is a small wooded valley
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is left exposed while climbing out of a little valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts K inside DEAN for DEKAN, which 'climbing' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed and uncovered both describe something bare, without clothing or protection.

clue.text: I gawk at thresher at sea, a predatory creature

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a thresher shark while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A thresher is itself a shark, which pulls the solver toward the wrong species; 'at sea' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The great white is a large ocean-going killer, a fish that hunts seals and other prey.

clue.text: Very hot current round mouth of river

indicators.note: round says one piece goes about the other

parts.note: topical means of current interest

indicators.note: the mouth of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A warm current flows around a river estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a flow of water, but it is the adjective, TOPICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Climates near the equator are hot and humid, so the word describes great heat.

clue.text: Arrived and got ready to play outside right

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: musicians tuned up before a performance

explanation.surface: A musician arrived and tuned the instrument, with someone outside on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or show up somewhere is an idiomatic way of saying arrived.

clue.text: A grant secured by the gymnast, maybe

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: A sports grant has been won by the gymnast.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast is one example of a sportsperson trained in physical exercises.

clue.text: Face a fine promenade

parts.note: F abbreviates fine, as on a pencil grade
a seafront walkway is called the front

explanation.surface: A seaside walk is described as lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the 'front' is the promenade running along a seaside town's shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront someone is to face them; an insult is also faced, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Female taking the part of male in mean con

indicators.note: taking the part of means standing in for, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a mean is a middle value

explanation.surface: An actress plays a man's role in a cheap swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like stingy, but it is the average, MIDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone by cheating is to fiddle them, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Volunteers reach island, one in the south Pacific

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to hit a target is to reach it
I abbreviates island, as on maps

explanation.surface: Volunteers arrive at a South Seas island.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve. 'island' looks like the definition but gives I; the definition is 'one in the south Pacific'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia, so it is one such place in that ocean.

clue.text: Came to study about revolutionary

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone came round to studying a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' looks like regaining consciousness, but it is arrived at.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place or total is to get there, the sense of the definition.

clue.text: Mountain cat almost catches a llama-like animal

indicators.note: catches means holds, so one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A mountain lion nearly catches a llama-like beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CAT to CA, and ALPCA then 'catches' A.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American camelid, bred for its wool, closely resembles a smaller llama.

clue.text: Show follows sort of blue film

indicators.note: follows puts the show's word after the shade of blue

parts.note: midnight blue is a very dark blue
to express is to show

explanation.surface: A show comes after a racy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue film' suggests something pornographic; the definition is just 'film'.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1978 Alan Parker prison drama set in Turkey has this title.

clue.text: Some criticism over turn

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some criticism is levelled at a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: In a board game such as chess, each player's go is called a turn.

clue.text: Forward pass not penalised at first

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of penalised

explanation.surface: A forward pass in rugby is not penalised at first.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a forward pass is a foul, so 'Forward pass' reads as one phrase; 'Forward' is the definition and 'pass' gives SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter or parcel is to dispatch it onward.

clue.text: Rogue failing to get in large country house

indicators.note: failing to get means the letters named are missing

parts.note: a villain is a rogue
taken as written

explanation.surface: A burglar fails to get into a country mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large house, especially one in the country or abroad.

clue.text: Criminal on the run casing Conservative Club

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so one piece wraps the other
criminal suggests something wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fugitive criminal cases a Tory political club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casing' sounds like a burglar sizing up a building, but it means enclosing C in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's baton is a short heavy club.
